Prepare ID for unique occurrences

Source: R/prepare_coord.R
prepare_coord.Rd

Adds an ID column identifying each unique location, and records which columns hold the coordinates, the household identifier and the interview date, so later steps (georef_coord(), summarise_by_interview()) find them without being told again.

Usage

prepare_coord(
  df,
  lat_var,
  lon_var,
  id = NULL,
  interview = NULL,
  id_rule = c("coordinates", "sequence"),
  digits = 5
)

Arguments

df

A data frame.

lat_var

variable with the latitude coordinate

lon_var

variable with the longitude coordinate

id

<tidy-select> Optional column identifying the survey units (households), recorded for later steps.

interview

<tidy-select> Optional column with the interview dates, recorded for later steps.

id_rule

"coordinates" (stable IDs) or "sequence".

digits

Decimals of the coordinates in a coordinate ID.

Value

A c4e_tbl: df with an ID column first, keyed by ID, with the survey's columns recorded.

Details

By default the ID is built from the coordinates themselves (longitude and latitude rounded to digits decimals, e.g. "30.12340_-0.54320"), so the same location gets the same ID in every wave, subset and run. With id_rule = "sequence" the IDs are "1", "2", ... in the order of the sorted coordinates, as in v1; they change whenever the set of locations changes.

Rows are sorted by latitude and longitude.

Examples

survey <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
prepare_coord(survey, lat_var = lat, lon_var = lon, id = hhid,
              interview = interview)
